text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — autoscaler probing strategy. We saw oscillation during tenant spikes when probes triggered eager scale-ups. Want to converge on a design that reduces thrash but still gives low tail latency for bursty tenants. TL;DR: prefer multi-stage probes + conservative admission.
jon: +1. From the staging runs: short 2s probes often looked successful but then failed under real traffic => rollback. Longer probes fixed flapping but cost a lot.
deepa: Proposal sketch: two-stage probing. 1) soft probe: ephemeral, CPU-only or 1 GPU-lite for 3s to validate traffic pattern. 2) confirm probe: reserve real slot for 20-30s before opening to full traffic. Keep soft probe cheap and rate-limited per-tenant.
kevin: We should combine that with exponential backoff and jitter for repeated failures so we don't hammer provisioning. Example config sketch:
```
probe:
  soft_duration: 3s
  confirm_duration: 30s
  max_concurrent_probes_per_tenant: 2
  backoff_intervals: [1m,2m,4m]
  jitter: 0.2
```
sara: Also need signals to validate success: probe_success_rate, time_to_warm, eviction_count_during_probe, and cost_delta_per_probe. Those should be in the dashboard.
maria: Good. Two operational questions: 1) who owns the decision logic (operator vs control-plane), 2) what are sane defaults for multi-tenant fairness?
jon: Operator-local decisions are faster for latency but we need global accounting to bill and cap warmups. Operator can make provisional admits; control-plane reconciles credits/limits and enforces daily quotas.
deepa: For fairness: enforce a small warmup-credit budget per tenant that replenishes slowly. Soft probes consume minimal credit; confirm probes consume more. If tenant is out of credits, fall back to model-variant or throttled admission.
alice: What about fragmentation/failure modes — e.g., confirm probe allocates GPU but then OOMs or fails due to GPU fragmentation?
deepa: Fallbacks: 1) try model-variant with lower memory (quantized/4-bit) for the confirm probe; 2) if that fails, spill to other region or queue the request with advisory TTL.
kevin: We should encode fallback priority list in the probe policy so operator can pick: [same-model-quantized, compatible-smaller-model, alternate-region]. Also add a probe admission timeout so confirm probes don't hold forever.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for autoscaler/probe-v2 on staging (tag: probe-v2-2026-03-22). Monitoring hooks added for probe_success_rate and probe_cost.
maria: Nice. A few more practical items: surface pending warmups/active probes in the console per-tenant (so SREs & customers see warmup queue), add alerts for high probe failure rate, and add tests that simulate noisy spike patterns.
jon: Agreed. Also add a README in the operator repo describing charge accounting for probes and how credits are topped up.
sara: I'll draft the dashboard panels and alert queries. Recommending these metrics: probe_success_rate (1m/5m), avg_time_to_confirm, probe_cost_1h, probe_failures_by_reason.
maria: Action items assigned: deepa -> RFC PR with probe schema + operator interfaces; kevin -> backoff/jitter impl + tests; sara -> dashboard; jon -> console surface ticket; maria -> canary plan and rollout window (2 weeks). Please tag me on PRs. :thumbsup:
alice: quick Q — do we permit tenants to opt out of probes and accept cold starts instead?
maria: Yes, opt-out should be supported at tenant config level (default on). Opt-out means no warmup credits used and higher latency SLA.
kevin: One more: add metric that attributes cost of confirm probe to tenant billing bucket so customers can see warmup cost.
maria: Perfect. If no major objections I'll open the RFC PR today and schedule the canary. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
